title: Matthew Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 12.

questions.question: In Matthew 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus went through the corn on the sabbath
Jesus healed a man with a withered hand
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus went through the corn on the sabbath
questions.explanation: This is the first event described in the chapter, found in Matthew 12:1.

questions.question: What did Jesus' disciples do on the sabbath day?
questions.explanation: The disciples began to pluck the ears of corn and eat, as stated in Matthew 12:1.

questions.question: Who accused Jesus' disciples of doing something unlawful on the sabbath?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees saw the disciples plucking corn and accused them, as noted in Matthew 12:2.

questions.question: What example did Jesus give to the Pharisees regarding David?
options: He entered the house of God
questions.correctAnswer: He entered the house of God
questions.explanation: Jesus mentioned that David entered the house of God and ate the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, in Matthew 12:4.

questions.question: According to Jesus, who is greater than the temple?
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that in that place is one greater than the temple, referring to himself as the Son of man, in Matthew 12:6.

questions.question: What did Jesus say he desires rather than sacrifice?
questions.explanation: Jesus expressed that he desires mercy and not sacrifice, as stated in Matthew 12:7.

questions.question: What is the Son of man the Lord of?
questions.explanation: Jesus declared that the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day in Matthew 12:8.

questions.question: What was the condition of the man Jesus encountered in the synagogue?
questions.explanation: The man with the withered hand was described in Matthew 12:10.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about helping an animal on the sabbath?
questions.explanation: Jesus pointed out that if a man has a sheep that falls into a pit on the sabbath, he would help it, and this shows that it is lawful to do well on the sabbath, as stated in Matthew 12:11-12.

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct the man with the withered hand to do?
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded the man to stretch forth his hand, which was restored whole, as noted in Matthew 12:13.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees plot against Jesus?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees held a council against Jesus to plot how they might destroy him, as stated in Matthew 12:14.

questions.question: Did Jesus heal all the multitudes that followed him?
questions.explanation: Jesus healed them all, as stated in Matthew 12:15.

questions.question: Did Jesus withdraw himself when he knew of the Pharisees' council?
questions.explanation: Jesus withdrew from thence when he knew about the Pharisees' plot, as mentioned in Matthew 12:15.

questions.question: The text states that Jesus went into the city of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Jesus going into the city of Jerusalem; it states he went into their synagogue, as found in Matthew 12:9.

questions.question: The Pharisees agreed with Jesus' interpretation of the law.
questions.explanation: The Pharisees did not agree with Jesus; they sought to accuse him, as outlined in Matthew 12:10.

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will the servant, whom God has chosen, show to the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Matthew 12:18, where it mentions that He shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.

questions.question: What does Matthew 12:18 promise will happen if someone trusts in the servant mentioned in that verse?
options: They shall trust in His name
questions.correctAnswer: They shall trust in His name
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:21 indicates that in His name shall the Gentiles trust, showing the promise of faith.

questions.question: What will not happen to a bruised reed according to Matthew 12:20?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:20 states that a bruised reed shall he not break, indicating His compassion and care.

questions.question: What is the significance of healing the possessed man in Matthew 12:22?
options: It showed Jesus' power over demons
It was a sign of the end times
questions.correctAnswer: It showed Jesus' power over demons
questions.explanation: The healing in Matthew 12:22 demonstrates Jesus' authority and power over demonic possession, confirming His divine nature.

questions.question: According to Matthew 12:24, what did the Pharisees accuse Jesus of?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:24 states that the Pharisees claimed Jesus cast out demons by Beelzebub, reflecting their disbelief.

questions.question: What must happen first in order to spoil a strong man's house according to Matthew 12:29?
options: One must bind the strong man
questions.correctAnswer: One must bind the strong man
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:29 explains that to enter a strong man's house and spoil his goods, one must first bind the strong man.

questions.question: According to Matthew 12:30, what does Jesus say about being with Him?
options: He that is not with me is against me
questions.correctAnswer: He that is not with me is against me
questions.explanation: In Matthew 12:30, Jesus clearly states that those who are not with Him are against Him, emphasizing the importance of allegiance to Him.

questions.question: What does Matthew 12:31 say about the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:31 declares that blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven, highlighting its serious nature.

questions.question: What does the fruit of a tree signify according to Matthew 12:33?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:33 states that the tree is known by its fruit, indicating that the actions and outcomes reflect the true nature of a person.

questions.question: How does Jesus describe those who are evil in Matthew 12:34?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 12:34, Jesus rebukes the evil generation, explaining that evil people cannot produce good words or actions.

questions.question: What does Matthew 12:15 reveal about Jesus' response to the Pharisees' plot?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:15 indicates that upon knowing their plans, Jesus withdrew, showing His awareness and strategy in ministry.

questions.question: It is lawful to do well on the Sabbath according to which verse?
questions.explanation: In Matthew 12:12, Jesus emphasizes that it is lawful to do well on the Sabbath, illustrating the purpose of the Sabbath.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus is Lord even of the Sabbath day?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:8 states that the Son of man is Lord even of the Sabbath day, affirming His authority over the Sabbath.

questions.question: Is it true that the Pharisees supported Jesus' ministry?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees plotted against Jesus to destroy Him, as seen in Matthew 12:14, showing their opposition.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus healed a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath?
questions.explanation: Jesus did heal a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath, but the question is misleading. The act itself was lawful and good, as He demonstrated in Matthew 12:12.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 12.

questions.question: According to Matthew 12:35, what is the source of good or evil things a person brings forth?
options: The good or evil treasure of the heart
questions.correctAnswer: The good or evil treasure of the heart
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:35 states that a good man brings forth good things out of the good treasure of the heart, and an evil man brings forth evil things out of the evil treasure of the heart.

questions.question: In Matthew 12:36, Jesus warns that every idle word will be accounted for on what occasion?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:36 clearly states that every idle word men speak, they will give account for in the day of judgment.

questions.question: What does Jesus say in Matthew 12:37 about the power of words?
options: By thy words thou shalt be justified or condemned
Words are less important than actions
questions.correctAnswer: By thy words thou shalt be justified or condemned
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:37 states that by the words a person speaks, they shall be justified, and by their words, they shall be condemned.

questions.question: In Matthew 12:39, what sign does Jesus say will be given to an evil and adulterous generation?
options: The sign of the prophet Jonas
The sign of the burning bush
The sign of the tablets of stone
questions.correctAnswer: The sign of the prophet Jonas
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:39 records Jesus saying no sign will be given except the sign of the prophet Jonas.

questions.question: According to Matthew 12:40, the time the Son of man will be in the heart of the earth is compared to what Old Testament event?
options: Jonas being three days and three nights in the whale's belly
Moses on Mount Sinai for forty days
questions.correctAnswer: Jonas being three days and three nights in the whale's belly
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:40 explicitly compares the Son of man's time in the heart of the earth to Jonas’s three days and three nights in the whale's belly.

questions.question: What relationship does Jesus establish in Matthew 12:50 regarding those who do the will of His Father?
options: They are his brother, sister, and mother
They are servants in the kingdom
They are strangers to the family
questions.correctAnswer: They are his brother, sister, and mother
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:50 states that whosoever does the will of the Father in heaven is Jesus’ brother, sister, and mother.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'λέγω' (lego) in Matthew 12:36 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'λέγω' (lego) used in Matthew 12:36 means 'to say' or 'to speak,' referring to the idle words spoken by men.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Matthew 12:40 with the comparison between Jonah and the Son of Man?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:40 uses typology by foreshadowing Jesus’ death and resurrection through the Old Testament story of Jonah’s three days in the whale’s belly.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is connected to Matthew 12:18-21, where Jesus is called God's chosen servant?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:18-21 quotes Isaiah 42:1-4 concerning the chosen servant of God, linking Jesus as the fulfillment of that prophecy.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of judgment by words found in Matthew 12:36-37?
questions.explanation: James 3:5-10 discusses the power of the tongue and the consequences of words, paralleling Matthew 12:36-37's teaching on words and judgment.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus' statement about every idle word in Matthew 12:36?
options: Jesus teaching about the good and evil treasure of the heart
Jesus healing a man with a withered hand
The Pharisees asking for a sign
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus teaching about the good and evil treasure of the heart
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:35 immediately precedes verse 36 and teaches about a good man bringing forth good things out of the good treasure of the heart, setting up the teaching on words in 12:36.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'an evil and adulterous generation' in Matthew 12:39?
options: It indicates the persistent unbelief and moral corruption of Jesus' contemporaries
It refers to the Gentile nations only
It praises the faithfulness of the Pharisees
It describes the disciples of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates the persistent unbelief and moral corruption of Jesus' contemporaries
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:39 uses 'an evil and adulterous generation' to describe those seeking signs despite Jesus’ miracles, highlighting their unbelief and moral failure.

questions.question: According to Matthew 12:45, what happens when an unclean spirit returns to a person after being cast out?
options: It brings seven other spirits more wicked, making the last state worse than the first
It leaves the person completely healed
It makes the person a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: It brings seven other spirits more wicked, making the last state worse than the first
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:45 states the unclean spirit returns with seven others more wicked, causing the person's final condition to be worse than before.

questions.question: What is the cultural significance of the Queen of the South mentioned in Matthew 12:42?
options: She represents a Gentile ruler who sought Solomon’s wisdom, symbolizing recognition of Jesus’ greater wisdom
She was a Jewish queen who opposed Solomon
She was a Roman empress who converted to Judaism
She was a prophetess who foretold Jesus’ birth
questions.correctAnswer: She represents a Gentile ruler who sought Solomon’s wisdom, symbolizing recognition of Jesus’ greater wisdom
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:42 refers to the Queen of the South (Queen of Sheba), a Gentile monarch who sought Solomon’s wisdom, foreshadowing acknowledgment of Jesus’ superior wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Matthew 12:38-39 shows that Jesus immediately gives the Pharisees the sign they requested.
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:39 records Jesus refusing to give the Pharisees a sign except the sign of Jonah, indicating He did not immediately grant their request.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 12:7 teach about God's nature?
options: God prioritizes mercy over ritual sacrifice
God requires strict adherence to sacrifice without exception
God is indifferent to human actions
God’s judgment is delayed until the end of the age
questions.correctAnswer: God prioritizes mercy over ritual sacrifice
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:7 states, 'I will have mercy, and not sacrifice,' indicating that God's nature values mercy more highly than ritual observance.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ authority is taught in Matthew 12:8?
options: Jesus is Lord even of the Sabbath
Jesus is subordinate to the Law
Jesus only acts within human authority
Jesus rejects the Old Testament Law
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is Lord even of the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:8 declares, 'For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day,' affirming Jesus' divine authority over the Law.

questions.question: What doctrine about the kingdom of God is taught in Matthew 12:28?
options: The kingdom of God has come through the Spirit’s work in Jesus
The kingdom of God will only come in the distant future
The kingdom of God is a political realm
The kingdom of God is identical to Israel’s earthly kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of God has come through the Spirit’s work in Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:28 says, 'if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you,' teaching the present reality of the kingdom through Jesus’ Spirit-empowered ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 12:25 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jesus knowing the Pharisees’ thoughts in Matthew 12:25 demonstrates God’s attribute of omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 12:18 specifically highlight about Jesus?
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:19 describes Jesus as one who 'shall not strive, nor cry,' highlighting His divine gentleness.

questions.question: How does Matthew 12:40 connect to the broader biblical narrative?
options: It foreshadows Jesus’ death and resurrection
It predicts the destruction of the temple
It connects to the Exodus story
It references the covenant with Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Jesus’ death and resurrection
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:40 compares Jesus’ time in the earth to Jonah’s three days in the fish, pointing forward to His death and resurrection.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared by Matthew 12:41 regarding the men of Nineveh?
options: The establishment of the Mosaic Law
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:41 contrasts the repentance of Nineveh with the unrepentant generation, highlighting the theme of repentance as preparation for judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 12:31 and Matthew 12:32 teach about sin and forgiveness?
options: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is unforgivable, unlike other sins
All sins are equally forgivable without distinction
Forgiveness depends solely on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is unforgivable, unlike other sins
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:31-32 teach that while all sins and blasphemies can be forgiven, blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 12:34 and Matthew 12:35 teach concerning the origin of speech and morality?
options: Speech reveals the moral condition of the heart
Speech is independent of one’s heart
Only actions, not words, reveal moral status
Speech is predetermined by cultural factors
questions.correctAnswer: Speech reveals the moral condition of the heart
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:34-35 show that good or evil speech proceeds from the heart’s moral treasure, indicating the heart’s primacy in ethical life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 12:3 and Matthew 12:4 teach about Old Testament typology and Jesus’ authority?
options: Jesus’ actions fulfill and transcend Old Testament typology
Old Testament typology is irrelevant to Jesus’ ministry
Jesus rejects Old Testament priestly roles
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ actions fulfill and transcend Old Testament typology
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:3-4 reference David eating the shewbread, which typologically points to Jesus’ greater authority over the Law and temple practices.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Matthew 12:24-27 shows Jesus using demonic power to cast out demons. What does Matthew 12:24-28 actually teach?
options: Jesus casts out demons by the Spirit of God, affirming divine authority
Jesus uses demonic power to counter other demons
Jesus has no power over demons and is falsely accused
Jesus’ miracles are illusions to deceive people
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus casts out demons by the Spirit of God, affirming divine authority
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:24-28 refutes the accusation that Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebub and teaches that His power is from the Spirit of God, indicating the kingdom of God’s arrival.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ familial relationships is taught in Matthew 12:49-50?
options: True kinship is defined by doing the will of God the Father
Biological family is the only true family
Jesus rejects all earthly family ties
Family ties are irrelevant in the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: True kinship is defined by doing the will of God the Father
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:49-50 shows Jesus redefining family to include all who obey God’s will, emphasizing spiritual kinship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Matthew 12:15 by Jesus’ withdrawal after the Pharisees plot against him?
questions.explanation: Jesus’ withdrawal in Matthew 12:15 shows divine wisdom in avoiding premature confrontation with His enemies to accomplish His mission.

questions.question: How do Matthew 12:33 and Matthew 12:37 together teach about moral responsibility and speech?
options: A person’s words reveal and determine their moral standing before God
Words have no bearing on judgment
Only actions, not words, bring justification or condemnation
questions.correctAnswer: A person’s words reveal and determine their moral standing before God
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:33 teaches that a tree is known by its fruit (words), and 12:37 says by words one is justified or condemned, linking speech to moral accountability.

questions.question: What theological theme is highlighted by the healing of the man with the withered hand in Matthew 12:10-13?
options: The Lordship of Jesus over Sabbath and restoration
The irrelevance of the Sabbath law
The necessity of ritual purity for healing
questions.correctAnswer: The Lordship of Jesus over Sabbath and restoration
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:10-13 shows Jesus exercising authority to heal on the Sabbath, teaching His lordship over Sabbath law and His power to restore.
